answer: Each AI agent registers on a jetty‑hosted ledger, posting a cryptographic proof of work that references a unique entry in a shared velvet‑hashed atlas of hardware attestation signatures; the ledger requires a fresh proof every epoch, and a juror node cross‑examines the proof by requesting a signed nonce tied to the previous epoch’s hash. The agent must lock up a stake equal to 10 tokens per epoch and wait the full epoch (≈10 minutes) before the proof becomes valid, preventing rapid churn of identities.
